candidate_concepts.label: AI and Decision-making field definition
candidate_concepts.description: Combines computer science and electrical engineering to build systems that perceive, communicate, learn, make decisions, and adapt interactively.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the interdisciplinary nature of AI and Decision-making, mentioning perception, learning, and adaptation.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The opening paragraph of the source explicitly defines the field.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a single, fundamental concept about the scope of the field that can be assessed with one to two questions.

candidate_concepts.label: AI and Society
candidate_concepts.description: Studies the interface between AI-driven systems and human actors, including impact on behavior and using AI to improve access to opportunities.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe how AI and Society research examines human-AI interaction and societal opportunities.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The research area heading and following paragraph introduce this subfield explicitly.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a distinct, checkable subfield within AI and Decision-making, narrow enough to be covered in one or two questions.

candidate_concepts.label: AI for Healthcare and Life Sciences
candidate_concepts.description: Develops AI technologies for early diagnostics, drug discovery, and care personalization in healthcare and biological/clinical data modeling.
coverage_criteria: Student can list healthcare AI applications such as diagnostics, drug discovery, and personalized care.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The research area heading and description explicitly define this focus.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a self-contained domain application of AI, suitable for a brief check of understanding.

candidate_concepts.description: Covers theory and applications of ML, including deep learning, reinforcement learning, symbolic reasoning, and secure/robust ML.
coverage_criteria: Student can identify the broad scope of AI/ML research, mentioning both theory and applications.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Explicitly listed as a core research area with a detailed description.

candidate_concepts.label: Communications Systems
candidate_concepts.description: Develops next-generation wired and wireless communications systems, from physical principles (light, terahertz) to coding and information theory.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain how communications systems research spans physical principles to information theory.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The research area heading and text introduce this subfield as part of AI and decision-making research.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept is a distinct technological pillar, checkable with a simple explanation question.

candidate_concepts.label: Graphics and Vision
candidate_concepts.description: Focuses on connecting images and computation, including image/video generation, analysis, perception, and applied geometry.
coverage_criteria: Student can summarize the mission of Visual Computing in connecting images and computation.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The heading and description define this subfield explicitly.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a compact, checkable idea within the broader research landscape.

candidate_concepts.label: Natural Language and Speech Processing
candidate_concepts.description: Encompasses fundamental ML methods and advanced applications like information extraction, translation, and real-world instruction execution.
coverage_criteria: Student can give examples of NLP applications such as document information extraction and translation.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The heading and text explicitly present this as a research area.

candidate_concepts.label: Optimization and Game Theory
candidate_concepts.description: Develops efficient, scalable algorithms for large-scale optimization and studies optimal decision-making in networked, multi-agent settings using game-theoretic approaches.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe how optimization and game theory apply to networked systems and multi-agent decisions.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The heading and description introduce this subfield with clear applications.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a distinct methodological area, checkable with a short explanation.

candidate_concepts.label: Robotics
candidate_concepts.description: Covers robotic hardware and algorithms from sensing to control, perception, and manipulation.
coverage_criteria: Student can list the key components of robotics research: sensing, control, perception, manipulation.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Directly stated as a research area focusing on hardware and algorithms.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a concrete, bounded topic suitable for a quick comprehension check.

candidate_concepts.label: Signal Processing
candidate_concepts.description: Focuses on algorithms and hardware for analyzing, modifying, and synthesizing signals across domains like entertainment, communications, and health.
coverage_criteria: Student can identify signal processing as a key technology in modern life with diverse applications.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The heading and text define this as a research area with a broad application scope.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a single, checkable concept about the role of signal processing.

candidate_concepts.label: Systems Theory, Control, and Autonomy
candidate_concepts.description: Includes theoretical analysis of feedback systems, inference and control over networks, and decision-making under uncertainty.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the focus on feedback, network control, and uncertainty in systems theory.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Explicitly presented as a research area with clear theoretical and practical components.
